overview.text: Ganesha is a Hindu deity widely revered as the son of Shiva and Parvati. Instantly recognizable by his elephant head and human body, he is worshipped as the remover of obstacles and lord of new beginnings; devotees invoke him before starting undertakings. One widely told story says Parvati made him to guard her door; after Shiva cut off his head in a confrontation, he restored Ganesha with an elephant’s head. Art often shows him with several arms, a broken tusk, and sweets, though stories and depictions vary. His continuing importance is reflected in regular worship and the Ganesha Chaturthi festival.

key_facts.text: Ganesha is identified by his elephant head and human body and is revered as a remover of obstacles and deity of new beginnings.
Devotees invoke Ganesha before beginning new undertakings; he is also associated with guarding doorways.
Accounts of how Ganesha got his elephant head differ. One commonly told story says Parvati created him to guard her door, and Shiva later restored him with an elephant’s head.
Sculptures may show Ganesha with multiple arms, a broken tusk, and sweets; the objects he holds can vary.
Ganesha Chaturthi is an annual festival honoring Ganesha; the Smithsonian describes celebrations that include processions and carrying images to the coast.
